payload: {"schema":1,"version":"0.0.58","date":"2026-11-03","lede":"Faster primitive editing: an optional raymarching shader draws clay primitives while you edit them, so moving them no longer rebuilds the clay every frame","highlights":["Faster primitive editing","Mirror a placed primitive"],"notesUrl":"https://klaysculpt.com/releases/0.0.58","windows":{"url":"https://github.com/c6ank/klay-releases/releases/download/0.0.58/Klay_Setup_0.0.58.exe","size":424122288,"sha512":"446cd00e4c7ecdbe83b42b7857442cefb2e2858035bd1c6d8ef6f7648345bba562caffd06a35a834109fb66e9e1e9cdc66700d0978af52779235d16e3cc29055"},"mac":{"version":"0.0.58","url":"https://github.com/c6ank/klay-releases/releases/download/0.0.58/Klay_0.0.58_macOS.dmg","size":558644662,"sha512":"1b015cc8b45507fb14956ab80ee81fbdc4d7e9b379f82392d3ce52fd6b86f997b6a5705ae6450866173199fdad4010816f175ce3358fece2d14f251dee8a737a"},"items":[{"g":"n","t":"Faster primitive editing","b":"With Raymarching when editing turned on, a clay layer of primitives is drawn by a raymarching shader while one of its primitives is moved, resized or edited, instead of rebuilding the clay every frame, so editing stays smooth with many primitives and with any material. When the edit stops, only the part of the clay that changed is rebuilt, once, and the layer is drawn from its mesh again; the selection outline stays visible throughout. The option is off by default; Raymarch all primitive layers in the same section draws these layers by raymarching at all times.","w":["Display settings \u203a Raymarching \u203a Raymarching when editing"]},{"g":"n","t":"Mirror a placed primitive","b":"The Primitives card has a Mirror section. Instance X, Y and Z add a linked mirrored copy of the selected primitive across the symmetry plane of that axis, and a second click removes it; editing either side changes both. With Follow symmetry on, turning symmetry on mirrors the selected primitive straight away.","w":["Primitives \u203a Mirror"]},{"g":"i","t":"Bevels keep their size when primitives are resized","b":"A primitive with a bevel or rounded edges keeps the same bevel on every side, at the same size, when it is made larger with the size handles, Scale X / Y / Z or the gizmo: a cube stretched into a rectangle keeps even edges, and a stretched disc or tube becomes a slot. The bevel only becomes smaller when the primitive is made smaller than its original size. On shapes with repeated details, such as gear teeth, text, bricks and window bars, the axes that cross those details still stretch as before.","w":["Tools \u203a Primitives"]},{"g":"i","t":"Primitive handles: move in a plane, resize one side","b":"The centre handle now matches the Gizmo tool: its dot moves the primitive in the screen plane, its ring scales it, and three plane dots move it within one plane (XY, YZ or ZX). Hold Shift while dragging a size handle to move only that side, while the opposite side stays in place; Ctrl now gives fine adjustment on size handles.","w":["Tools \u203a Primitives"]},{"g":"i","t":"Pin the outliner's Display and Transform windows","b":"The Display window (opened from an object's icon) and the Transform window of the outliner now have a title bar like the Blending window: drag it to move the window anywhere, including over the viewport. The pin button beside the close button keeps the window open; clicking another object's icon or transform button then shows that object in the same window. The Transform window now updates once an edit is finished rather than during it.","w":["Outliner \u203a Object icon / Transform"]},{"g":"i","t":"More blends for Subtract and Intersect, Type and curve on every blend","b":"Muscle, Groove, Weld, Inflate, Columns, Stairs, Split edge, Noisy, Sag and Stretch now also work with Subtract and Intersect, shaping the rim of the cut; Weld, Muscle and Inflate still add material there. The blend Type (Smooth, Chamfer, Soft, Circular, Silky, Exact) now changes the Columns, Stairs, Pipe, Muscle and Inflate blends too: Chamfer gives diamond pleats, bevelled steps or a diamond tube, and the other types round them differently. The Type row is hidden on Chamfer and Morph, where it has no effect. The profile curve is available on every blend except Chamfer, Pipe and Morph: with the Smooth type it sets the shape of the join, and on Inflate the shape of the puff. Each blend of a primitive now keeps the last values you gave it, also after restarting Klay; Reset blend returns it to its defaults.","w":["Outliner \u203a Blending"]},{"g":"i","t":"Primitive noise through Noise layers only","b":"The Primitives card no longer has the Surface and Noise advanced sections; noise and patterns are added with Noise layers. A primitive from an older scene that already has a surface noise still shows those sections, so the noise can be edited or removed.","w":["Tools \u203a Primitives \u203a Noise layers"]},{"g":"f","t":"Resizing the tool card in the sidebar by its top handle no longer stutters in scenes with many layers."},{"g":"f","t":"The Swap shape list now opens at the selected primitive's shape and highlights it, instead of at the top."},{"g":"f","t":"Dragging a slider on the Primitives card, or moving, rotating or scaling a primitive in the viewport, no longer makes the viewport stutter."}],"history":[{"version":"0.0.57","date":"2026-11-02","lede":"Clay paint colour and material from the toolbar, and Klay starts again on AMD Radeon RX 5000 and RX 6000 cards","highlights":["Clay paint colour and material","Colour for clay primitives","Noise layers for primitives"],"notesUrl":"https://klaysculpt.com/releases/0.0.57","items":[{"g":"n","t":"Clay paint colour and material","b":"The clay row of the toolbar has a Color tile between Stamp and Stencil, showing the paint on a small lit ball; click it to turn the paint on or off. Hover it to pick a colour, and use the palette's expand button or the tile's label for the Clay paint panel: colour, albedo, roughness, metal and emission, strength, softening, jitter or a gradient along the stroke, and colour smudging. From surface picks the colour of painted clay with a click, and pen pressure can drive the albedo strength, the jitter amount or the gradient colour. Painted clay no longer tints the rest of the model, and brushes that drip, such as Melting, carry the paint they drip from, tinted by the paint colour at its strength. The palette and the panel can be pinned and moved, and the colour cell of the zen Brush pastille opens the same palette and panel.","w":["Toolbar \u203a Clay \u203a Color"]},{"g":"n","t":"Colour for clay primitives","b":"Clay primitives have a Color section with three switches: Albedo with a colour, Roughness and Metalness, each with its value. Where two coloured primitives meet, the colours blend across the join, mixed as pigment or linearly like Clay paint; a subtracted primitive gives its colour to the cut. The colour is stored as the layer's clay paint, so it can be tuned in the Material tab with the new vertex channel sliders, and it stays when the layer is sculpted, merged into the sculpt or converted to poly, where roughness and metalness now carry over as well.","w":["Tools \u203a Primitives \u203a Color"]},{"g":"n","t":"Noise layers for primitives","b":"The Primitives card has a Noise layers section that stacks further noises and patterns over the Surface noise, listed like the Flood tab's processes, with the top row applied last and an icon for each noise or pattern type. Each layer has its own noise or pattern settings, an opacity, a blend mode such as Add, Subtract, Max, Smooth max or Mask below, and a Where setting that limits it to peaks, cavities, upward or side-facing surfaces, or to the layer below. Warp above bends every layer placed over it. Rows are reordered by dragging their handle, the type is chosen from a searchable list with icons, and each layer's settings sit in a Parameters section that folds away. Layers apply to Clay and Poly primitives and are saved with the scene and with variants. Noise amount now goes up to 1, five times the previous limit.","w":["Tools \u203a Primitives \u203a Noise layers"]},{"g":"i","t":"Clearer mode switcher on the toolbar","b":"The Clay, Polygone, Mask and Paint buttons now show one fixed icon each: a circle, a triangle, a square with a dot and a palette. The active mode's icon is filled, and the active brush is shown only in the brush row beside it. This applies to the full and the zen toolbar.","w":["Toolbar \u203a Modes"]},{"g":"i","t":"Primitives for hard-surface work","b":"Tapping Shift+A, or clicking the + tile, adds the current shape with its edited settings. By default it is placed at the scene centre, or at the centre of the selected clay layer, aligned to the world axes; the Placement card's Quick add at option can place it at the cursor or at the selected object's pivot instead. Holding Shift+A opens the full primitive list. Right-clicking a shape in that list sets it as the default primitive, which is the shape the tool starts with, or adds it to the favourites. The Primitives card has a Transform section with position, rotation and size, and buttons that reset the position to the world origin and the rotation to the world axes. The same Transform menu opens from a primitive's row in the outliner. In the Handles card, Right-drag rotates can be turned off so the right mouse button always orbits the view. A clay primitive placed in an empty selected clay layer always goes into that layer, which moves to the primitive if it was placed outside it. A primitive placed outside the selected clay layer gets its own new layer, centred on it, at the same resolution. In the Swap shape panel, the shape list now folds away like the Blending section, and the Join panel is now named Blending.","w":["Tools \u203a Primitives"]},{"g":"i","t":"Subsurface radius from the surface colour","b":"The Subsurface section of a PBR material has a Radius from albedo switch. When it is on, the scatter distance of each colour channel follows the surface colour, including texture maps and vertex paint, instead of the Radius colour. It applies in the viewport; Raytrace support will follow.","w":["Material \u203a PBR \u203a Subsurface \u203a Radius from albedo"]},{"g":"i","t":"Expand or collapse every section of a tool card","b":"Right-clicking the body of the tool card in the sidebar opens a menu with Expand all and Collapse all, which open or close every folding section of that card at once. The Primitives card now opens with only its top section expanded; in Box and Lasso modes, only the first section is expanded.","w":["Sidebar \u203a Tool card \u203a Right-click"]},{"g":"f","t":"Undo on clay could skip a stroke and undo the one before it instead, and sculpting where the skipped stroke was could then break the clay into blocks. Every stroke is now recorded and undone in order."},{"g":"f","t":"Klay closed during startup on AMD Radeon RX 5000 and RX 6000 series graphics cards. It now starts normally on these cards (hopefully)."},{"g":"f","t":"Voxelize with detail projection could leave holes in the result, and the holes grew while sculpting it. The result is now complete."},{"g":"f","t":"Selecting a MatCap material could close Klay."},{"g":"f","t":"The Fill tool did not offer some visible holes, most often on voxelized meshes with deleted faces. It now finds holes whose border runs past a flipped or non-manifold face."},{"g":"f","t":"With Void navigation on and Pan set to Alt and the left button, dragging on empty space panned instead of orbiting, and releasing Alt mid-drag did not zoom. Dragging on empty space now orbits, and Alt keeps its own pan and release-to-zoom behaviour."}]},{"version":"0.0.56","date":"2026-11-01","lede":"Merging clay layers no longer leaves missing patches up close","highlights":["Merged clay layers are complete up close","Smooth Boolean / Merge of rotated layers","Align moves only the clicked clay primitive","Brush value drag on left / middle mouse"],"notesUrl":"https://klaysculpt.com/releases/0.0.56","items":[{"g":"f","t":"Merging two clay layers, or uniting them with Boolean, could leave missing patches of surface that showed only up close. The merged layer is now complete."},{"g":"f","t":"A clay Boolean or Merge of a rotated or rescaled layer could leave pinholes and short raised lines along the voxel grid. The result is now smooth and closed."},{"g":"f","t":"The Align tool now moves only the clay primitive you click, as it does an object, instead of the whole clay layer that holds it. Two primitives of the same clay layer can also be aligned onto each other."},{"g":"f","t":"On clay layers, resizing the Smooth brush while holding Shift now keeps the new size after Shift is released, when the Smooth brush uses the primary brush size."}]},{"version":"0.0.55","date":"2026-11-01","lede":"Faster, lighter clay: sculpting up to 5x faster on half the memory; a Primitives tool with 133 parametric shapes for Poly and Clay; Color correct looks in the Library; Smooth or Handles curves with a live dab preview; Sharp retopology hits its polycount with clean open borders","highlights":["Faster, lighter clay","Primitives tool","Point instancing in instance packs","Clay layer resolution","Color correct looks","More ways to blend clay"],"notesUrl":"https://klaysculpt.com/releases/0.0.55","items":[{"g":"n","t":"Faster, lighter clay","b":"Clay sculpting is up to four to five times faster and a clay object uses about half the video memory, so larger and more detailed clay fits on the same card. Large strokes now release without a pause.","w":["Clay layers"]},{"g":"n","t":"Primitives tool","b":"A new Primitives tool places 133 parametric shapes, from boxes, gears and knots to rocks, architecture parts and fractals, as a poly mesh or as clay. Click places a shape on the surface and handles adjust its size and parameters; the card adds deform, symmetry, surface noise and boolean settings, plus a Box mode for shaping a cube and a Lasso mode that inflates a drawn outline. On a clay layer each shape is listed in the outliner, where its blend, order and grouping can be edited.","w":["Tools \u203a Primitives"]},{"g":"n","t":"Point instancing in instance packs","b":"An instance pack holds copies of one or more objects as points, far beyond the previous limit of about a thousand copies per scene, and draws them faster than the same number of separate copies. Instance point adds the selection as a point to the current pack, or creates a pack when there is none; move the new point and press it again within five seconds to repeat the move. Create > Instance pack makes an empty pack and Add to pack chooses the target pack, the outliner lists each object of a pack with its own visibility, and a single point can be selected, moved, duplicated or removed. Packs work with poly and clay objects, shadows and the path tracer, and Ctrl+D still makes a separate copy.","w":["Right-click \u203a Copy \u203a Instance point"]},{"g":"n","t":"Clay layer resolution","b":"Each clay layer has a resolution of Low, Default, High, Ultra or Extreme, chosen from the capsule beside its name in the outliner, which also shows the layer's scale in its colour. Clay layers now also show a rendered thumbnail on their outliner card, like poly meshes, refreshed when you switch to another layer. A higher resolution gives a bigger box at the same detail; Extreme is meant for graphics cards with plenty of memory, a lower one cuts the clay outside the smaller box after asking first, and Undo restores it.","w":["Outliner \u203a Clay layer \u203a Resolution"]},{"g":"n","t":"Color correct looks","b":"The Library has a Color correct category of saved looks, each shown on the same grey sphere so they compare side by side. Click a look to apply it to the Post process; turn off Click applies to select with a click and apply with a double-click. Every Color correct panel (Post, the Camera Grade panel and the picture viewer) now has Copy, Paste and Save at the top, and shows the name of the look last applied.","w":["Library \u203a Color correct"]},{"g":"n","t":"More ways to blend clay","b":"The clay Boolean panel's Blending section adds Inset, Extrude, Line groove, Tongue, Repel and Avoid, which press, raise or engrave one object into another or make the objects give way to each other. A folded More blends section holds twelve further joins: Columns, Stairs, Pipe and Split edge for hard surfaces, Noisy, Sag, Stretch and Bridge for organic joins, and Exclude, Morph, Shell and Replace. A Type switch under the tiles sets how every join is rounded: Smooth, Chamfer, or, from the \u22ef button, Soft, Circular, Silky and Exact. The same joins and types are available on the shapes of a clay layer made with the Primitives tool, from the outliner's Join card, whose Blending section can be folded to keep only the Union, Subtract and Intersect switch, and from the right-click Join menu.","w":["Boolean \u203a Clay \u203a Blending"]},{"g":"n","t":"Zen toolbar","b":"A compact, icon-only bottom toolbar: the round dot at the right end of the toolbar switches to it, the short bar at its right end switches back, and Ctrl+T (Cmd+T on macOS) switches between the two. Names and shortcuts appear on hover, and the brush drawer and the tools list open above it. Drag either arrow sideways to show more or fewer brushes or tools; hold a brush or a tool to drag it to a new place, as on the full toolbar. The full toolbar's brush arrow, and a new arrow on its Tools card, resize the same way.","w":["Bottom toolbar \u203a Zen toolbar"]},{"g":"n","t":"Brush pastille","b":"An optional column on the left of the viewport for the Zen toolbar, turned on by right-clicking the toolbar: Radius and Strength sit at the top, followed by any functions, brush settings, Stamp, Falloff, Stencil, dividers, switches and folders you add with Add function. Right-click the pastille to add, reorder or remove items.","w":["Zen toolbar \u203a right-click \u203a Brush pastille"]},{"g":"n","t":"Folds growth for stamp brushes","b":"The stamp brush's Growth section has a Branches | Folds switch. With Folds, holding the brush on a clay layer grows a folded, organic surface from a small ball or from the clay under the brush. The clay itself changes smoothly at frame rate while you hold, at a steady pace that does not depend on the frame rate (about seven seconds to the Stop at size), with folds kept thick enough that the surface stays closed, and releasing it keeps the result as one undo step; Esc during the hold restores the clay. Grown from the clay under the brush, the folds become the clay's own surface, with no second surface left underneath, so they can also turn inward into the clay; grown from a ball, the growth is added onto the clay. Dragging the brush seeds new growth along the whole stroke, anywhere on the layer, at the brush's spacing. The new Frill, Lettuce, Coral, Fine coral, Brain and Swell stamp brushes are set up for it. Settle after freezes older growth away from the growing edges so it no longer counts toward Max points, which lets the edges keep growing during long holds.","w":["Brush \u203a Growth \u203a Folds"]},{"g":"n","t":"Volume texture for clay brushes","b":"Any clay brush can project a grayscale image through the clay with triplanar mapping, on top of what the brush already does. Strength sets how much it acts. Add raises the light parts and sinks the dark ones, Carve only digs the dark parts in, and Break cuts the brush's own deposit where the image is dark, so the stroke lands as broken chunks. Map, Triplanar and Cells offer the same controls as the Flood tab's Displace texture.","w":["Brush \u203a Noise & patterns \u203a Volume texture"]},{"g":"n","t":"Crease and rake in clay","b":"The clay Elastique brush can now crease and rake clay live: drag across the surface to fold the clay ahead of the brush and leave a clean groove behind it, from a soft valley to a knife-sharp crease or a raised ridge. The groove's profile, depth and width respond to pen pressure, and Slide warp lets the surface stretch and bunch around it like skin. Holding Ctrl, or turning on Invert brush, raises the same profile out of the surface instead of cutting it. Dab length sets how often the groove is laid down, so a shorter step follows quick turns closely.","w":["Brush \u203a Elastique \u203a Surface slide"]},{"g":"n","t":"Poly brushes in the Clay tab","b":"Right-click a brush in the toolbar's Poly tab and choose Copy to Clay preset to add a copy of it to the Clay tab, where it sculpts clay layers with the same behaviour. The copy is a separate preset: changing its settings does not affect the original brush.","w":["Toolbar \u203a Poly \u203a right-click \u203a Copy to Clay preset"]},{"g":"n","t":"Smooth or Handles curves","b":"Every curve editor has a Smooth | Handles switch under the graph. Smooth keeps the current behaviour. Handles draws B\u00e9zier segments whose handles follow the points automatically; drag a handle to bend that point by hand, and right-click the handle to make it automatic again. Points and handles highlight under the cursor. The mode and any bent handles are saved with each curve. The area under the curve is now filled, and the brush Falloff curve shows a live preview of the dab above it that updates while you drag a point.","w":["Brush \u203a Falloff curve"]},{"g":"f","t":"The gizmo now scales a clay layer evenly on all three axes. Scaling a clay layer along one axis, which distorted the clay, is no longer offered."},{"g":"f","t":"The installer no longer refuses to install when an earlier Klay was removed by deleting its folder. It now clears the leftover entry and continues, and if an earlier version cannot be uninstalled it offers to install over it."},{"g":"f","t":"In VR through Virtual Desktop, the headset image no longer looks darker than the viewport. If another VR runtime shows the headset too dark or too bright, the VR window's Headset output setting changes how the image is handed to it."},{"g":"f","t":"A Laser cut with fill through parts that pass into each other, such as fingers resting on a palm, crossing strands or an unmerged sculpt, now fills each part cleanly. The fill previously could leave holes or flipped faces at the seam. These cuts are also faster."},{"g":"f","t":"After many Move strokes on a clay object, patches of the surface no longer disappear where you pulled. They previously stayed missing until a Smooth stroke passed over them."},{"g":"f","t":"The clay Elastique brush now shows its Compressibility while you drag, so the surface no longer shifts slightly when you release."},{"g":"f","t":"With symmetry on, the dot that marks the mirrored brush position is now hidden when it is behind the model."},{"g":"f","t":"The Mirror tool's cut keeps quads where the mirror plane crosses a row of quads. The centre seam previously became a strip of triangles."},{"g":"f","t":"Sharp retopology now produces close to the polycount you set. It previously gave about a third of the target on the starter head (around 1,900 faces for 5,000)."},{"g":"f","t":"After a gizmo Align, scaling along one axis no longer distorts the model and no longer makes the gizmo disappear. Align now turns the green axis to the picked face."},{"g":"f","t":"Undoing or redoing a gizmo move, rotation or scale now brings the gizmo back with the object. It previously stayed where the drag had ended."},{"g":"f","t":"Selecting with V now works on clay objects the same way as on poly: a drag box selects every clay object it covers, a single one becomes the active layer, and a V click no longer creates a new clay layer."},{"g":"f","t":"After a Boolean between a clay object and a poly mesh, deleting another clay object no longer leaves a copy of the used clay object in the viewport that could not be selected in the outliner or deleted. Undo now also restores that clay object correctly."},{"g":"f","t":"Redo after undoing a Laser cut on a clay object now restores the cut exactly. It could previously bring back a damaged surface."},{"g":"f","t":"Voxelize now shows only the finished result, with its detail projected. The bare voxel shell no longer appears for a moment before the detail."},{"g":"f","t":"Favourites in the library are no longer limited: pinning a new one no longer removes the oldest. Clicking the Stamp or Falloff tile on the toolbar shows every favourite in a grid."},{"g":"f","t":"On a narrow Library window the header buttons no longer run under the Size slider: Import, Save current, Click applies and Re-render all now sit on their own row under the header, with Size at its right."},{"g":"f","t":"The Library button in the top bar now reopens the Library on the category you last used, including after a restart. It previously always opened on Clay stamps."},{"g":"f","t":"Video memory is released after you subdivide a mesh to a high level. About 1 GB used to stay reserved for the rest of the session, even after a new scene or with only a small model left."},{"g":"f","t":"Boolean and Blend results on clay objects now keep each object's surface smooth. The preview and the applied result could previously show blocky bumps over the whole surface, away from the join."},{"g":"f","t":"With symmetry on, clay brushes with Elastique or Surface slide now
